name: Blur Highlight

height.note: 0 means the copy's own height - in a page this is a paragraph, not a stage. The gallery and the Video page set one so the card has something to centre

blur.note: how far out of focus the copy starts

rise.note: how far it lifts as it sharpens. 0 by default: the copy arriving in place, rather than travelling, is what keeps this readable as text and not as an entrance

direction.note: which way the highlighter runs. `center` opens from the middle of each phrase in both directions at once

accent.note: the highlighter colour, from the Continia palette only. `auto` is Innovation Blue in both themes

stagger.note: between one mark and the next. 0 draws them all together, which is what makes a paragraph read as one marked thought rather than as a list

gap.note: between the copy landing sharp and the first mark. The order is the whole idea - a highlight over a blur is decorating something nobody can read yet

hold.note: how long the finished paragraph stands before it replays

loop.note: false plays it once when it scrolls into view and leaves it finished - the right setting in real copy

autoplay.note: play when it scrolls into view

reducedMotion: The paragraph is copy with phrases marked in it, so under reduced motion it is simply already there: sharp, fully highlighted, no loop. Nothing is withheld - the marks are content, not decoration, and a reader who has asked for less motion still needs to see which phrases carry the point.
notPorted: the per-character reveal. The reference offers a character-level variant; this one works at the paragraph, because a blur applied per character costs a filter per glyph and the effect reads the same from a metre away.

the reference's default highlight colours (#FF9FFC light, #7C3AED dark). Both are off the Continia palette, and neither is a tint of anything in it, so the default is Innovation Blue and the alternatives are the other three brand colours.
brandNotes: Not a port. The source is React Bits Pro: the code is behind a subscription and its licence (§2.4) forbids putting the source in a repository or making it available to third parties. This repo is public and ships dist/ as a reusable bundle, so none of it may enter here. This entry is built from scratch on the Continia tokens from the public docs page and a screen recording; sourceUrl is provenance, not a source file. The one deliberate difference beyond the palette is the markup contract: the phrases are <mark> elements rather than a prop, so the paragraph still means what it says with the JS absent.
blurb: A paragraph that arrives out of focus, pulls sharp, and then draws a highlighter across the phrases that carry the point. The order is the idea: the copy is readable before anything in it is marked.
demo: Continia is built inside Business Central, so approvals, document capture and payments happen where the finance team already works - not in another system to log in to.
